title: IP-MT287-InlineAiEditGhostTextSeam

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the Antigravity / Cursor-class inline AI-edit EDITOR SEAM in the native code editor — the ghost-text preview of a proposed AI edit shown inline (as dim virtual text for an insertion, or a red-strike/green-insert inline diff for a replacement) with Tab-to-accept, Esc-to-reject, and Alt-] / Alt-[ to cycle alternatives. PARITY HERE IS THE EDITOR SEAM, NOT THE MODEL: this MT owns the render + accept/reject + apply-as-one-undo, and consumes AI-proposed edits as typed EditProposals delivered through the WP-017 Pillar-A session API (MT-007 AgentSessionService: launch/steer/status). The MT-281 matrix marks 'ai-inline-edit-ghost-text' MISSING: editor_view has LSP CompletionPopup only; there is no ghost-text inline-edit overlay and no proposal accept/reject path wired to the agent session runtime. This MT does NOT call a model directly, does NOT own prompting, and does NOT implement completion inference — it defines the typed EditProposal seam and the editor UI that renders and applies it; the producer is an agent session via MT-007.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) NEW module dir src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/inline_ai/ with mod.rs, proposal.rs (typed EditProposal + EditProposalStream client seam consuming MT-007 session output; NO model call), ghost_render.rs (the ghost-text / inline-diff renderer over the virtualized layout), session.rs (InlineAiState: pending proposal, alternatives, accept/reject/cycle state machine); (b) `pub mod inline_ai;` + re-exports in code_editor/mod.rs; (c) wiring in code_editor/panel.rs: a 'Request Inline Edit' trigger (default Ctrl+K, Antigravity/Cursor parity) that sends the current selection/context to the bound agent session and enters proposal-preview mode, Tab-accept / Esc-reject / Alt-]-Alt-[ cycle, and apply-as-one-undo; (d) one integration test file driving the seam with a FAKE proposal stream (no live model). Consumes MT-007 (SC-MT007-SessionApiSurface); NO backend model code; NO new inference.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. proposal.rs: `pub struct EditProposal { proposal_id: Uuid, session_id: String, kind: EditProposalKind, range: (usize,usize) (byte range in the current buffer the edit replaces; empty range = pure insertion at a point), new_text: String, rationale: Option<String>, alternative_index: usize, alternative_count: usize }`; `pub enum EditProposalKind { Insertion, Replacement, MultiRangeReplacement(Vec<(usize,usize,String)>) }`. `pub trait EditProposalStream { fn poll(&mut self) -> ProposalPoll; }` where ProposalPoll = Pending | Ready(Vec<EditProposal>) | Error(String) | Done. The PRODUCTION stream adapts MT-007 session output (the agent proposes edits as structured session messages); this MT ships the trait + a test fake. NO model call, NO prompt construction here — the seam is transport-only.
2. ghost_render.rs: for an Insertion, render new_text as dim virtual (ghost) text at the point (not in the buffer), theme-token muted color, wrapping across lines correctly in the virtualized layout (MT-002 show_rows). For a Replacement, render an inline diff: the replaced range shown with a strike/removed style and the new_text shown with an added style directly adjacent (VS Code inline-suggestion + Cursor inline-diff visual), so the operator sees exactly what changes. MultiRange shows each changed span with the same treatment. Ghost text is NEVER in the buffer until accepted and is non-selectable decoration.
3. session.rs: InlineAiState { pending: Option<EditProposal>, alternatives: Vec<EditProposal>, active: usize, phase: Idle|Requested|Previewing|Applying|Error }. Ctrl+K -> Requested (send selection + surrounding context to the bound agent session via MT-007 steer/launch; the CONTEXT PAYLOAD build reuses MT-288's context-attach if present, else a minimal selection+file payload) -> on proposals arriving -> Previewing (render the active alternative as ghost/inline-diff). Tab accepts the active proposal: apply new_text to range as ONE undo entry (MT-035/051 single-undo boundary) and clear the state. Esc rejects: discard all proposals, restore the pristine view, and emit a typed 'rejected' outcome back to the session (so the agent knows). Alt-] / Alt-[ cycle alternative_index and re-render. A proposal whose range no longer matches the buffer (the buffer changed since the proposal was made) is INVALIDATED, not applied to a shifted range — it is dropped with a visible 'edit no longer applies' note (never silently applied to the wrong place).
4. Provenance + safety (binding): an accepted inline AI edit is attributed as model-authored in the same edit ledger the rest of the editor uses (the edit description carries the session_id / robot id) so accepted AI edits are auditable, matching the WP-017 provenance discipline (operator vs model authorship must never blur). The seam NEVER auto-accepts: acceptance is always an explicit operator Tab (or a governed auto-accept flag that defaults OFF and is out of scope here).
5. AccessKit: the ghost overlay is a Role::Group `code_editor_inline_ai` (instance-suffixed per panel.rs RISK-004) with a Role::Label `code_editor_inline_ai_preview` carrying the proposal text for the a11y tree, and an accept/reject hint `code_editor_inline_ai_hint`. Ghost text must be exposed to AccessKit as a distinct proposed-edit node, not as buffer content, so a screen reader / agent never mistakes a preview for committed text.
6. Scope edges: this MT is the EDITOR SEAM only. It does NOT implement the model, the prompt, or inference; it does NOT own the agent chat dock (MT-098) or the multi-file review flow (WP-017 WM/NA). It consumes EditProposals from an agent session (MT-007) and renders/accepts/rejects them.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the WP-017 MT-007 contract (AgentSessionService launch/steer/status DTOs, the /agent-sessions routes, session output shape) as the proposal producer; code_editor/editor_view.rs (CompletionPopup — the ghost overlay must be DISTINCT from LSP completions and not fight them); panel.rs (virtualized per-line paint, single-undo boundary, off-thread drain, RISK-004 instance-suffix ids, edit description/ledger); buffer.rs/cursor.rs (byte-range apply); keymap.rs (add RequestInlineEdit Ctrl+K, AcceptInlineEdit=Tab-in-preview, RejectInlineEdit=Esc, CycleAlt chords).
2. Create inline_ai/proposal.rs (EditProposal types + EditProposalStream trait + a test fake); NO model/prompt code.
3. Create inline_ai/ghost_render.rs (ghost text for insertion, inline diff for replacement, over the virtualized layout, theme tokens) + inline_ai/session.rs (the Idle..Error state machine + accept-as-one-undo + reject-emits-outcome + cycle + range-invalidation).
4. Wire panel.rs: Ctrl+K enters Requested and sends context to the bound session (MT-007); render the active proposal; Tab/Esc/Alt-]/Alt-[ handling; accepted edit carries model provenance in its ledger description.
5. Register `pub mod inline_ai;` + re-exports in code_editor/mod.rs.
6. Integration test (FAKE stream, no live model): request -> single insertion proposal renders as ghost text -> Tab accepts as one undo; a replacement proposal renders as inline diff -> Esc rejects and restores + emits 'rejected'; two alternatives cycle with Alt-]/Alt-[; a proposal whose range drifted (buffer edited mid-preview) is invalidated with the note, not misapplied; accepted edit's ledger description contains the session/model id. Capture Argus screenshot + AccessKit tree of a ghost insertion, an inline-diff replacement, and the accept/reject hint.
7. Update the UserManual (same change): inline AI edit — Ctrl+K to request, ghost/inline-diff preview, Tab accept / Esc reject / Alt-] Alt-[ cycle, that previews are never in the file until accepted, and that accepted AI edits are recorded as model-authored.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/** (the agent session runtime is MT-007 / Pillar-A; this MT consumes it, never edits it or adds model/inference code)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/editor_view.rs (LSP completions stay separate; the ghost overlay must not modify the completion popup)
acceptance_criteria: code_editor/inline_ai/ exists with proposal.rs (typed EditProposal{proposal_id,session_id,kind,range,new_text,rationale,alt index/count} + EditProposalKind Insertion/Replacement/MultiRangeReplacement + EditProposalStream trait + a test fake), ghost_render.rs (ghost text for insertion, inline diff for replacement over the virtualized layout), session.rs (Idle..Error state machine).

The seam consumes EditProposals produced by a WP-017 agent session (MT-007) and contains NO model call, NO prompt construction, and NO inference (grep-provable: no reqwest to a model endpoint, no completion inference in inline_ai/**).

Ctrl+K requests an inline edit (sends selection + context to the bound session); the active proposal renders as ghost text (insertion) or inline diff (replacement) that is NEVER in the buffer and is non-selectable decoration (theme-token colors, no hardcoded hex).
Tab accepts the active proposal as ONE undo entry; Esc rejects, restores the pristine view, and emits a typed 'rejected' outcome to the session; Alt-] / Alt-[ cycle alternatives.
A proposal whose byte range no longer matches the buffer (edited mid-preview) is INVALIDATED with a visible 'edit no longer applies' note and never applied to a shifted range.
An accepted inline AI edit is recorded as model-authored (its edit-ledger description carries the session/robot id); the seam never auto-accepts (acceptance is an explicit operator action).
AccessKit exposes the ghost overlay as a distinct proposed-edit node (code_editor_inline_ai / _preview / _hint), instance-suffixed, so a preview is never mistaken for committed buffer text.
UserManual updated in the same change: Ctrl+K request, ghost/inline-diff preview, Tab/Esc/Alt-] Alt-[ semantics, previews-not-in-file, AI edits recorded as model-authored.
proof_targets: Argus evidence: argus.screenshot + AccessKit tree of (a) a ghost-text insertion preview, (b) an inline-diff replacement preview, (c) the accept/reject hint, stored under $HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT
code_surfaces: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs (Ctrl+K request + preview + Tab/Esc/Alt cycle + one-undo apply + model provenance)
expected_tests: unit: EditProposal apply — insertion at a point vs replacement of a range produces the correct buffer text
unit: ghost/inline-diff render model for insertion, replacement, and multi-range
unit: AccessKit exposes the preview as a proposed-edit node distinct from buffer text
integration: Ctrl+K request -> fake stream single insertion -> Tab accept as one undo
integration: replacement proposal -> Esc reject restores view + emits 'rejected' outcome
integration: two alternatives cycle with Alt-]/Alt-[
integration: range-drift proposal invalidated with the note, not misapplied
integration: accepted edit's ledger description carries the session/model id (model provenance)
implementation_notes: Verified grounding 2026-07-21: WP-017 MT-007 (SC-MT007-SessionApiSurface) defines AgentSessionService with launch/steer/interrupt/status and /agent-sessions routes + typed DTOs — the proposal producer. code_editor/editor_view.rs has CompletionPopup (LSP) which the ghost overlay must stay distinct from (both can be visible; Tab semantics must not collide — inline-AI Tab-accept only in Previewing phase). panel.rs owns the virtualized per-line paint, single-undo boundary (MT-035/051), off-thread drain, RISK-004 instance-suffix ids, and the edit-ledger description (for model provenance). MT-284 snippets also uses Tab; the two must arbitrate Tab by active phase.

Design basis (cite in code docs): Antigravity / Cursor / GitHub Copilot inline suggestion + inline edit (Ctrl+K) — ghost text for a completion, an inline red/green diff for an edit, Tab accept, Esc reject, Alt-] cycle. PARITY IS THE SEAM: the render + accept/reject + apply, not the model.

PROVENANCE IS LOAD-BEARING (WP-017 discipline): an accepted AI edit must be recorded as model-authored so operator vs model authorship never blurs — reuse the same edit-ledger description path the rest of the editor uses, tagging the session/robot id.

The context payload sent on Ctrl+K reuses MT-288 (agent-editor-context-attach) when available; if MT-288 has not landed, send a minimal selection+file+language payload through the MT-007 steer path. Do NOT build a prompt here — the agent session owns prompting.

Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-288 supplies richer context; MT-098 chat dock is the conversational surface; WP-017 WM/NA own multi-file agent-edit review; AC/NA annotations are a distinct feedback (not-an-edit) channel.

target_entries: Inline AI edit: Ctrl+K to request, ghost-text / inline-diff preview, Tab accept / Esc reject / Alt-] Alt-[ cycle, previews are never in the file until accepted, and accepted AI edits are recorded as model-authored

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Proposal accept/reject outcomes and the model-authored apply are recorded as auditable events (session/robot id) so the provenance of an AI edit is traceable; the reject outcome is emitted back to the session.

The InlineAiState phase, active alternative, and invalidation reason are exposed as structured state for the visual_debugger so a no-context model can trace why a proposal was previewed, applied, rejected, or invalidated.
The seam consumes an agent session (MT-007 owns supervision/liveness of the producing session); this editor overlay spawns no child process of its own.

risk_if_missed: The native editor has no AI-inline-edit seam, so the Antigravity/Cursor headline affordance — preview an AI change in place and accept or reject it with one keystroke, with the model kept separate from the editor — is impossible, and there is no auditable, provenance-tagged path for an agent to propose an edit the operator reviews inline.

risks: RISK-1: Silent auto-apply — a proposal is applied to the buffer without an explicit operator accept, letting model text enter the file unreviewed.
RISK-2: Provenance laundering — an accepted AI edit is recorded as operator-authored (or unattributed), blurring operator vs model authorship in the edit ledger.
RISK-3: Range drift misapplication — the buffer changes after the proposal was made and the edit applies to a shifted range, corrupting unrelated code.
RISK-4: Preview mistaken for buffer — ghost text is exposed as real buffer content to AccessKit / copy, so a screen reader or an agent reads a not-yet-accepted preview as committed code.
RISK-5: Tab collision — inline-AI Tab-accept fights LSP completion Tab or snippet Tab, so Tab does the wrong thing.
RISK-6: Scope creep into the model — the seam starts constructing prompts / calling a model directly, violating the model/editor separation and the orchestrator-no-inference boundary.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Acceptance requires an explicit operator action; there is no auto-accept path in this MT. A test asserts a proposal never mutates the buffer until Tab.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Accepted edits carry the session/robot id in their ledger description; a test asserts the model-authored attribution on an accepted proposal.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): A proposal whose range no longer matches is invalidated (not re-anchored/misapplied); a test edits mid-preview and asserts the proposal is dropped with the note.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Ghost text is non-selectable decoration exposed to AccessKit as a distinct proposed-edit node; a test asserts it is not in the buffer text and copy does not include it.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Tab-accept is active only in the Previewing phase; a test with an open LSP completion and with an active snippet asserts Tab arbitration is correct.

CTRL-6 (RISK-6): The seam is transport-only (EditProposalStream); a grep proof asserts no model endpoint / prompt-template / inference code in inline_ai/**; proposals come only from the MT-007 session.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-native-editors-v1: code_editor/editor_view.rs has only the LSP CompletionPopup (no ghost-text inline-edit overlay); no inline_ai module; interop/interaction_bus.rs carries clipboard/selection, not agent proposals. WP-017 MT-007 (SC-MT007-SessionApiSurface, read in this packet) defines the AgentSessionService launch/steer/status seam that produces proposals. Confirmed 'ai-inline-edit-ghost-text' is not covered by WP-012 (MT-001..108, incl. MT-098 chat dock which is conversational, not inline-edit), WP-013/014 stubs, STUDIO, or WP-011. External design basis: Antigravity / Cursor / Copilot inline suggestion + Ctrl+K inline edit.
corrections: Parity here is explicitly the EDITOR SEAM, not the model: the gap is the ghost-text/inline-diff preview + accept/reject + provenance-tagged apply wired to the WP-017 session API (MT-007), NOT model inference (which the agent session owns). The chat dock (MT-098) is a distinct conversational surface and does not close this gap.
